the ECAL has a good performance and that it is well suited for the detection of cosmic rays in the GeV to TeV energy region.
the AMS-02 lead scintillating fibber Electromagnetic Caloriemeter has been designed and built, and has been tested in beam tests with electrons and protons with energies up to 250  GeV.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (i) the calorimetric response and energy resolution of the AMS-ECAL, (ii) the electron/proton and photon/hadron rejection capabilities of the calorimeter, (iii) the calorimeter performance as standalone photon trigger, (iv) the calorimeter response to cosmic ray muons, (v) the calorimeter radiation hardness, (vi) the calorimeter stability and ageing.
the design of the calorimeter, its mechanical assembly and the electronics.
the development of a high precision, fine-grained, sampling calorimeter for the measurement of electrons, photons and positrons with the AMS-02 space mission.

the AMS-02 ECAL is a high-performance calorimeter with an excellent energy resolution and a very high electron/hadron separation capability.
all the requirements for a successful mission have been fulfilled.
the ECAL is fully ready for the launch in May 2011.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AMS-02 ECAL was successfully designed and built, and it is now flying in space since May 2011.
the AMS-02 ECAL is ready to fly and has a high potential to provide important physics measurements.
the ECAL has been designed and tested to meet the requirements of the experiment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ECAL is a well understood detector with excellent performance and a good understanding of the physics of the detector.
the ECAL performance is in agreement with our Monte Carlo predictions.
the ECAL is capable of providing a good energy resolution and electron/hadron separation, and that the calorimeter is robust and reliable.
